newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen higher at start.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen higher at start.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to move higher at the start of trading Thursday, following through on a broad rally which took the Dow industrials above 7,000 for the first time in almost seven weeks.
But analysts said that the market would remain a prisoner of economic data due out Thursday and Friday and that even a fast start could dissolve into profit-taking later in the day.
"If the numbers are bening, we could continue the rally," said Hildegard Zagorski, analyst at Prudential Securities."
"But even if we rally in the morning, we will face profit-taking in the afternoon ahead of the (April) employment report on Friday," Zagorski said.
March personal income and consumption are due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT as are weekly jobless claims. The April NAPM is due at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT as is March construction spending.

"I'm wary of this rally, even though it is broad and the volume is good," Zagorski said. "I just think that this market has come up such a long way that I have doubts about how much farther it can go. Also, some analysts think rates will be raised despite sluggish data."
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average was up 124.21 points, or 0.65 percent, to 19,275.33.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was up 3.9 at 4439.9.
U.S. shares were at a virtual standstill in London due to the closure of most European financial markets in observance of the May day holiday.
The dollar jumped to 127.45 yen in Tokyo and slipped agains the mark and yen in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were thinly mixed, with the long bond up 2/32 to yield 6.95.

The New York Times Market Place writes that better-than-expected corporate profits and relief that strong economic growth has not induced inflation cause the Dow Jones Industrial Average to power higher. But the news could have another side: this same strong economic growth could be just what prompts the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates again, even if the inflation data are still subdued.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that the question making the rounds is whether Sanford Weill was about to leave the bargain basement to make a full-price acquisition.
The legendary deal maker and cost cutter is scouting for acquisition possibilities for Travelers Group Inc.
